title: Toll relief $60 weekly cap – Terms and Conditions
summary: This page outlines the terms and conditions for the Toll relief weekly cap, which helps reduce the cost of toll spending.
who_can_apply: Must be registered in NSW for private use.
Must have been charged as a Class A Vehicle and not as a Class B vehicle (unless the vehicle is a Business Vehicle).
Must not be a Business Vehicle.
Must be eligible for the scheme based on the specific dates: 2024 and 2025 (1 January to 31 December); 2026 (1 January to 1 December).
what_you_need: Your toll account number from your toll service provider (E-Toll or Linkt).
One of the vehicle licence plate numbers listed on your toll account.
Your contact email address listed on your toll account.

internal_links.text: Claim the toll relief – $60 toll cap

faqs.q: How is the toll relief calculated?
faqs.a: On toll spend between $60 and $400 a week per tag and/or licence plate number, every dollar spent after $60 will be reimbursed up to a maximum of $340. For example, if you spend $65, you are reimbursed $5, and if you spend $400 or more, you are reimbursed a maximum of $340.

faqs.q: How often is the toll relief claimed?
faqs.a: The relief is calculated once a quarter. Any quarterly rebates that are not claimed will continue to accrue until the Claim period closure.

faqs.q: What is the maximum amount that can be reimbursed?
faqs.a: The maximum reimbursement is $340, which applies when the toll spend is $400 or more.
